stemBlocks.value: AB is a diameter of the circle shown on the grid, with A(-5, 2) and B(3, -4). (a) Determine the coordinates of the centre C. (b) Calculate the length AB. (c) Hence state the radius. (d) Verify that the point D(4, -1) lies on the circle by calculating the length CD.
Think first: The centre of a circle is the midpoint of any diameter, so read A and B off the grid first and everything else follows.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the centre as the midpoint of AB.
Find AB with the distance formula.
Halve the diameter to get the radius.
Find CD from C(-1, -1) to D(4, -1).

contentBlocks.value: CD = 5 = r, so D is exactly one radius from the centre
Result: D lies on the circle

strategyBlocks.value: Read A and B from the graph, use the midpoint formula for the centre and the distance formula for AB, halve AB for the radius, then test D by comparing CD with the radius.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) C(-1, -1)  (b) AB = 10 units  (c) radius = 5 units  (d) CD = 5 units = radius, so D(4, -1) lies on the circle.

whyThisWorks.value: A circle is the set of all points a fixed distance — the radius — from one fixed point. That single fact does all the work here: the diameter passes through the centre, so its midpoint is the centre; the radius is half the diameter; and any point is on the circle exactly when its distance from the centre equals that radius. Checking membership of a circle is therefore always a distance calculation, never a guess from the picture.
